title: RunSet
description: An evaluation over more than one resource, exactly as `RunSet.to_dict()` emits it. A directory is a stable input shape whether it holds one document today and fifty tomorrow, so its result is an envelope rather than a bare list. Described as it is: two field names disagree with the Run envelope and that is recorded here rather than corrected.

resources.description: How many resources were observed. It cannot say how many the identity failed to return, and `run_coverage` is where that limit is recorded rather than inferred.

by_class.description: Resource class to how many carried it. A label, never a filter.

set_aside.description: How many runs a profile moved BELOW THE FOLD. Not how many were skipped: their findings are evaluated, counted and printed, just lower down. This said 'set aside rather than evaluated', which is the opposite of what the engine does, and a consumer implementing the contract as written would report evaluated resources as unevaluated.

run_coverage.description: The same idea a Run calls `coverage`, under a different name. `expected` is deliberately optional here: counting documents proves how many resources were observed and never how many were missed, so its absence is stored as not-established rather than as complete coverage.

runs.description: Each run whole. Duplicate resource ids are refused at construction, because two documents describing one resource is a collection defect and not a set of two.

$schema.description: The exact contract this document claims, which must be the $id of the schema validating it. An instance convention and not the dialect keyword: inside a schema document `$schema` names the JSON Schema dialect, and using one field for both meanings is what this separation exists to prevent. It replaces `schema_version`, which was a second version that could not even express the one in the $id — `1.0` against a contract ending in `/1.2.0` — and was maintained by hand.
